{{short description|British veterinary researcher}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''(Dorothy) Claire Wathes''' née '''Bulman''' (born 1953) is a British [[Veterinary medicine|veterinary]] researcher who studies the [[reproduction]] of farm animals. She is known for her work on [[infertility]] in dairy cattle. As of 2018, she is a professor of veterinary reproduction at the [[Royal Veterinary College]] in [[Hatfield, Hertfordshire|Hatfield]].<ref name=RVC_bio />

==Education and career==
Wathes gained a BSc in zoology from the [[University of Birmingham]] in 1974.<ref name=RVC_bio /><ref name=SRF_2010>{{citation |url=http://srf-reproduction.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/2010-SRF-Annual-Conference-Final-Programme-Nottingham.pdf |title= Conference 2010 |publisher=[[Society for Reproduction and Fertility]] |date=2010 |accessdate=21 March 2018}}</ref> Her PhD on [[fertility]] in dairy cattle was from the [[University of Nottingham]] in 1978, under the supervision of [[Eric Lamming]];<ref name=RVC_bio>{{citation |url=https://www.rvc.ac.uk/about/our-people/claire-wathes |title=Professor Claire Wathes |publisher=[[Royal Veterinary College]] |accessdate=20 March 2018}}</ref><ref name=RSB /> her thesis was entitled "Progesterone levels and fertility of lactating cows".<ref name=Lamming_ch>GE Lamming. "[https://books.google.com/books?id=gOUgBQAAQBAJ&pg=PA351 Reproduction during lactation]", pp 335–53, in ''Control of Ovulation'', DB Crighton, GR Foxcroft, NB Haynes, eds, (Butterworth-Heinemann; 2013) ({{ISBN|1483162710}}</ref> In 1990, she was awarded a DSc by the [[University of Bristol]].<ref name=RVC_bio /><ref name=SRF />

Her first postdoctoral post was at the [[Babraham Institute]] in [[Cambridge]]. From 1979 to 1990, she worked in the [[University of Bristol]]'s Department of Anatomy, holding positions successively as lecturer and reader, before rejoining the Babraham Institute as a project leader (1990–94). She has been professor of veterinary reproduction at the [[Royal Veterinary College]] since 1994, leading the college's Reproduction and Development Group from 1995 to 2007.<ref name=RVC_bio /><ref name=SRF_2010 /><ref name=RSB /> She also holds a guest professorship at [[Huazhong Agricultural University]] in China (since 2009).<ref name=RVC_bio /><ref name=SRF />

From 2000 to 2008, Wathes chaired "ARK-Genomics", the steering committee of the [[Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council]] Investigating Gene Function Initiative for livestock,<ref name=RVC_bio /><ref name=RSB /> which aimed to facilitate [[genomics]] research across the UK.<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.bbsrc.ac.uk/documents/genomics-evaluation-report-pdf/ |title=Evaluation of BBSRC 'genomics' research |publisher=[[Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council]] |date=May 2011 |accessdate=21 March 2018 }}</ref> She became the first director of the Farm Animal Genetics and Genomics Faraday Partnership in 2002, and she continues to serve on a committee of its successor body, the Knowledge Transfer Network.<ref name=RVC_bio /><ref name=RSB /> She also served on the veterinary advisory committee of the [[Horserace Betting Levy Board]] (from 1997 until 2006 or 2008).<ref name=RVC_bio /><ref name=RSB />

==Research==
The long-term focus of Wathes' research has been [[reproduction]] in domestic [[ruminant]]s, including cattle and sheep.<ref name=RVC_bio /> [[Fertility]] in dairy cattle, and the problem of infertility, have formed an important part of her work from the outset. In her early research in Nottingham, with Lamming and others, she developed a method to diagnose and monitor low fertility in cows by measuring levels of the [[progesterone]] [[hormone]] in their milk.<ref name=RVC_bio /><ref name=Lamming_ch /> Her subsequent research at the Royal Veterinary College has investigated what causes cows to have low fertility, including their [[genotype|genetic background]], [[nutrition]] and [[metabolism|metabolic]] status, as well as [[bacterial infection]] of the [[uterus]] after calving.<ref name=RVC_bio /><ref name=Wellcome>{{citation |url=https://blog.wellcome.ac.uk/2012/11/23/milk-metabolism-and-making-it-pay/ |title=Milk, metabolism and making it pay |author=Holly Story |publisher=[[Wellcome Trust]] |date=23 November 2012 |accessdate=21 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170610150100/https://blog.wellcome.ac.uk/2012/11/23/milk-metabolism-and-making-it-pay/ |archive-date=10 June 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref> She has shown that lack of sufficient nutrients is an important cause of infertility.<ref name=Wellcome />

While working at Bristol she showed, with Ray Swann, that the [[oxytocin]] hormone is produced in the [[corpus luteum]] of the [[ovary]] in sheep and other ruminants, as well as in the [[neurohypophysis]].<ref name=RVC_bio /><ref name=Heap_Flint>[[Brian Heap|RB Heap]], APF Flint. "[https://books.google.com/books?id=AzwXjtcE-CEC&pg=PA156 Pregnancy]", pp. 153–59, in ''Hormonal Control of Reproduction'', CR Austin, RV Short, eds, 2nd edn (Cambridge University Press; 1984) ({{ISBN|0521275946}})</ref> This might form part of the mechanism by which female ruminants detect whether or not they have conceived.<ref name=Heap_Flint /> She has subsequently studied how hormonal and other factors regulate the [[estrus cycle|oestrus cycle]] and the [[birth]]ing process in sheep and cows.<ref name=RVC_bio />

==Awards and societies==
Wathes is an elected fellow of the [[Royal Agricultural Society of England]] (RASE) and the [[Royal Society of Biology]].<ref name=SRF /> She has served on the council of the Royal Society of Biology since 2017, and has also held roles on the committees of several other learned societies, including the European Society of Domestic Animal Reproduction, the [[Society for Endocrinology]] and the [[Society for Reproduction and Fertility]].<ref name=RSB>{{citation |url=https://www.rsb.org.uk/about-us/governance/council |title=Council Members |publisher=[[Royal Society of Biology]] |accessdate=20 March 2018 }}</ref>

Her awards include RASE's Research Medal (2006) for her work on fertility in dairy cattle, and the Society for Reproduction and Fertility's Marshall Medal (2015).<ref name=RSB /><ref name=SRF>{{citation |url=http://srf-reproduction.org/wp-content/uploads/2016/07/SRF2016-M-Medallist-C-Wathes.pdf |title=SRF 2015 Marshall Medalist |publisher=[[Society for Reproduction and Fertility]] |accessdate=21 March 2018 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
She was married to [[Christopher Wathes]], also a veterinary researcher; he died in 2016.<ref>{{citation |url= https://www.ufaw.org.uk/ufaw-medal-for-outstanding-contributions-to-animal-welfare-science/ufaw-medal-for-outstanding-contributions-to-animal-welfare-science-past-awards |title=UFAW Medal for Outstanding Contributions to Animal Welfare Science |publisher=[[Universities Federation for Animal Welfare]] |accessdate=21 March 2018}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
*DC Bulman, GE Lamming (1978). Milk progesterone levels in relation to conception, repeat breeding and factors influencing acyclicity in dairy cows. ''[[Journal of Reproduction and Fertility]]'' 54: 447–58 {{doi|10.1530/jrf.0.0540447}}
*DC Wathes, RW Swann (1982). Is oxytocin an ovarian hormone? ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' 297: 225–27 {{doi|10.1038/297225a0}}
*DC Wathes, DRE Abayasekara, RJ Aitken (2007). Polyunsaturated fatty acids in male and female reproduction. ''[[Biology of Reproduction]]'', 77: 190–201 {{doi|10.1095/biolreprod.107.060558}}
*DC Wathes, Z Cheng, W Chowdhury ''et al''. (2009). Negative energy balance alters global gene expression and immune responses in the uterus of postpartum dairy cows. ''Physiological Genomics'' 39: 1–13 {{doi|10.1152/physiolgenomics.00064.2009}}
